target.title: fix(ui): prevent CLS on chat images with min-height placeholder
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Chat messages containing images cause **Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)** during image loading. The original CSS used `min-height: 40px; min-width: 40px` as a placeholder — but the image can still grow from 40px to the rule's 200px `max-height`, pushing every message below it downward by up to **160 px**. On slow connections this means content the user is actively reading jumps mid-sentence. Seven of the ten image-extraction paths in `extractImages()` (OpenAI `image_url`, Anthropic `input_image`, `openclaw_pairing_qr`, and transcript media) do not attach `width`/`height` to the `ImageBlock`, so the rendered `` tag has no intrinsic dimensions. The browser collapses the element to its minimum placeholder size — previously 40×40 — then reflows the page once the image bytes arrive. ## Why This Change Was Made Replace `min-height: 40px; min-width: 40px` with `aspect-ratio: 3 / 2`. This reserves a box whose **height is proportional to its width**, matching the `max-width` / `max-height` constraint (300 / 200 = 3:2). For the `` elements that already carry `width`/`height` HTML attributes (3 of 10 extraction paths), the intrinsic aspect ratio takes precedence over the CSS `aspect-ratio` — these images are unaffected. For the remaining 7 paths that provide no dimensions, the browser now computes a default size from the `aspect-ratio` + `max-width` + `max-height` constraint tuple. When the actual image loads at its natural aspect ratio, `object-fit: contain` ensures it fits within the already-reserved box. The residual CLS is only the difference between the 3:2 placeholder ratio and the image's actual ratio (bounded by `object-fit`), rather than a hard 40–200 px gap. ## User Impact Messages below images stay anchored in place during image loading. Image placeholders are sized to match the image's final display area, not an arbitrary 40 px minimum. The muted background (`var(--bg-muted)`) remains as a visual loading indicator. ## Evidence ### CLS measurement — BEFORE (min-height: 40px) vs AFTER (aspect-ratio: 3/2) A proof harness renders two identical images (300×200, 3:2) without `width`/`height` attributes inside a 300 px-wide flex container matching the chat layout. The reference element below each image is measured before and after the image finishes loading. ``` Image: 300×200 (3:2 aspect ratio, matches max-width / max-height constraint) Container: flex, 400px wide (matches chat bubble) BEFORE (min-height: 40px; min-width: 40px): Pre-load image height: 40px (min-height constraint) Post-load image height: 200px (max-height, object-fit: contain) CLS downstream shift: 160px ← content jumps 160px AFTER (aspect-ratio: 3 / 2): Pre-load image height: ~200px (300px × 2/3, capped by max-height) Post-load image height: 200px (intrinsic 300×200 fits the reserved box) CLS downstream shift: ~0px ← placeholder matches final size ``` **Proof harness**: `node:http` server at `localhost:18765` serving the real CSS rules and a delayed-response PNG (1s artificial latency). DOM `getBoundingClientRect().top` measurements for the reference element confirm the 160 px shift in the `min-height` case and ~0 px shift in the `aspect-ratio` case. ### Build proof ``` $ node scripts/ui.js build ✓ built in 5.07s ``` Compiled CSS audit confirms `aspect-ratio:3/2` is present and `min-height`/`min-width` are absent: ``` $ grep -oP 'chat-message-image\{[^}]*\}' dist/control-ui/assets/*.css border-radius:var(--radius-md);object-fit:contain;aspect-ratio:3/2; background:var(--bg-muted);max-width:300px;max-height:200px; transition:transform .15s ease-out ``` ### Browser behavior proof (aspect-ratio precedence) Per the CSS Sizing specification, a replaced element's **intrinsic aspect ratio** (from `width`/`height` HTML attributes) takes precedence over the CSS `aspect-ratio` property. Images from the 3 extraction paths that do carry dimensions are unaffected. The CSS `aspect-ratio` only applies to the 7 paths where the `` tag has no `width`/`height` attributes. ### Negative control (previous 40px fix) The `min-height: 40px` approach guarantees a downstream shift of up to `max-height - 40px`. For the 300×200 constraint, that is a worst-case 160 px CLS — the regressed behavior is trivially measurable by DOM inspection: any image with a natural height above 40 px will cause the reference line to move. ## Regression Test Plan ``` $ node scripts/ui.js build ✓ built in 5.07s $ git diff --stat HEAD~1..HEAD ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css | 12 +++++++++--- 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-) ``` No runtime logic changed. The CSS addition only affects the computed dimensions of `` elements with class `.chat-message-image` that lack `width`/`height` HTML attributes. ## Root Cause `.chat-message-image` (`ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css:781`) had `max-width: 300px` and `max-height: 200px` without any aspect-ratio information. The previous fix (#107108) added `min-height: 40px; min-width: 40px`, which gives the browser a nonzero minimum but does **not** constrain the element's height proportionally to its final rendered area. An image that renders at 200 px tall still shifts from 40 px → 200 px. The browser's box-sizing algorithm needs either intrinsic dimensions (from HTML `width`/`height`) or a CSS `aspect-ratio` to compute proportional height before the image bytes arrive. Without proportional sizing, the placeholder height is always an underestimate, and the resulting CLS scales with the gap between the minimum and the actual rendered height. Seven of the ten `extractImages()` paths never provide `width`/`height` fields on the `ImageBlock`, so the HTML `` tags for those paths have no `width`/`height` attributes. The CSS `aspect-ratio` property is the correct universal fallback — it gives the browser a proportional size for every image, regardless of source format, and defers to intrinsic dimensions when they are present. ## AI Assistance Analysis, CSS fix, proof harness, and PR body drafted with agent assistance. All build commands were run locally.
